digest.component_or_area: LLM gate economics and cost analysis
propositions: Mean cost per completed ticket is $11.85 (median ~$8.15, p90 ~$21) since the Bedrock switch; per-gate costs are plan-review $3.02, code-review $1.42, completion-verification $2.24 per run.

Cheap-model experiments (rounds 1-6) tested Nova Pro, Nova 2 Lite, and Haiku; Nova Pro reduces per-run finder cost 30-40x ($0.07-0.09 vs $2.31-3.00) but with only 50-57% blocking-criteria recall; Haiku achieves parity on completion-verification (19/22 vs Sonnet 22/22) with $0.40 vs $1.20 banked-run cost but over-strict on certain case types.

Code-review severity axes are structurally inert because blocking is routed by criterion (only `security` criterion has blocking_enabled=True for 98.2% of findings) and the 0.95 impact threshold is mathematically unreachable (max observed impact 0.90, requiring impossible 3-way AND on blast_radius=system AND likelihood=high AND reversibility=hard); the ordinal-to-binary migration must fix threshold/aggregation before validation.

Ordinal-migration plan phases 0-3 identified: Phase 0 removes unused base-five emissions, Phase 1 converts undecomposable criteria to binary kind-sets (plan-v5), Phase 2 replaces plan-review ordinal ladders with deterministic binary derivation (plan-v6), Phase 3 addresses code-review via 3,230-finding verification corpus.

Nova ceilings fix (e800) and overlap_drain redesign (0-findings history across 2,093 plan reviews) are landed; overlap-judge batch and single-path bugs (confidence 0.0 and 1024-output truncation) found in ticket cumbersome-littlish-koalabear (PASSED plan-review, signed/claimable).

Two Bedrock false-positive defect families identified in observability.sh: widespread-zealous-narwhal (cold-start offset seeding on new counters) and colossal-slothful-grouse (over-broad marker pattern matching in review-bot prose); 77 Nova client errors on 2026-08-10/11 fully explained by MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS ceilings (e800 fix landed).
